criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Read per frame at full size and at 432 px. Frames 1, 3 and 9 pass most of the showstopper test. One white tractor sits in a pool on a near-black field with true blacks (slide 1's median L* is 0.8 per art_preflight). Slide 9's twenty tractors in white stalls against primer rows are a countable close. Several middle frames fall back on defaults, though, and that puts the deck below the 7 descriptor, which allows only one such frame. Slide 4: twenty front-on bobtails sit in a thin band (y about 1020 to 1460 of 2000 display px) and read as icons in a row. The bottom quarter is an empty dark dead zone. The tonal step the flow critic logged at y 625 still runs behind dek lines 2 and 3 as a lighter horizon band. Slide 5: at feed size the rule reads as six flat mid-grey tiles with a bracket over them, close to the UI slider the storyboard itself named as a risk. The grooves have little visible depth, and the steel face sits in the grey middle even after the darkening this round. Slide 6: the loss bar is a pebbled navy rectangle filling a box, with a leftover hairline across its middle at y about 1375. The billet is a 14 px sliver, and an empty dark band runs from y 700 to 1000. In the 432 px thumb it reads as a filled bar-chart rectangle, not mill-scale steel. Slide 8: the recompose is bolder and fills the frame, but the cab and trailer are lit lavender-blue against the neutral flood of frames 1 to 4 and 9, and the lit flank is camera-left. The trailer front is a flat primitive slab across the left third (crop r2c1), and the beacon dome is dimmer than the headlamp. Slide 7 is the best relief: Texas reads, the white inlay and the primer stud line are distinct materials with casts, and the label is clear of the routes. The county borders still read as stair-stepped ridges. Slide 2 reads as a mechanism, but its chassis models are slabs: blank approach pads and a door that is a flat black rectangle. The 'scale configuration' leader still crosses the house roof. Type sits on true dark quiet on every frame and no frame uses a plate.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Clearly one deck. It is one floodlit night world from one chassis, and one tractor recurs on 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 and 9. Rust primer has exactly one meaning, 'said, not yet done', on 3 (stop bar), 5 (clamp), 6 ($9M tick), 7 (studs and the New Braunfels punch) and 9 (stalls), which makes it a working motif. The camera move from apron to oblique to gate, yard, cab and mast is declared and visible. The value holds dark throughout with no strobe. Three things hold it under 8. Slide 8's lavender key and camera-left lit flank put it outside the deck's one light. The 5 to 6 relief pair cuts from spatial night scenes to flat orthographic grey panels, a declared value cut that lands as a change of medium more than a turn. The same front-on kit grille faces the camera on five frames (flow_craft cross_frame 'a').

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every slide numeral traces to the claims file, all primary from the SEC-filed letter or Aurora's own release: 20+ (c1), 500,000, 100% and September (c2), 20 trucks a week in early December (c11), $3M (c13), $257M including SBC (c14), about $9M for 2026 and six weeks (c12), 500 trucks and 2027 and 2028 (c3, c4), non-binding (c19), 200 by end of February (c15), 1,000+ by end of 2027 (c16), five-year (c20) and October 28th. The Dallas to Laredo line is kept as Charger's plan and Dallas to Houston as Aurora's own route (c21), which matches the rejections. Two looser points. First, the storyboard says the station and gate are 'labelled as illustrations', and no such label appears on slides 1 to 3. Only slide 7 says its routes are drawn straight. Second, the $9M tick on slide 6 is measured from the billet's left edge (tick at about x 165 display, billet at 123, bar scale about 5.0 px per $1M). The brief says it starts 'from the datum's left end', but the datum bleeds off frame, so the encoding's zero isn't visible to a reader. Neither one changes what a reader believes, and neither is a hard fail.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened (Aurora's Q3 letter: weigh station traversal, ramp slip, money), where (Dallas to Houston, Dallas to Laredo, New Braunfels on slide 7) and who decided (Aurora, plus FMCSA's exemption on slide 8). Nothing is named for what a reader can do next, and no Texas body or deadline appears. The closing question in the caption is the only handle. The stake that driverless trucks now cross Texas scales unattended is stated generally.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe, slide 2 pays the mechanism at once and the turn at 5 ('About six weeks behind its own plan') is where understanding changes. Slide 9 closes on built against expected. Slide 8 (the beacon) sits between the map and the close and could move without loss. The flow critic's not_done list proposes moving it to position 3.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register with no banned words, and 'by Aurora's own count' on slide 4 is a good, honest line. It reads as a careful wire reporter, not as a Texan who knows weigh stations. 'The letter says' recurs on 2, 4, 5 and 8, and nothing on the frames carries regional texture past the place names on slide 7.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: A floodlit night weigh station is new against nos. 64 to 66 (art_preflight distinct_from_recent). Familiar moves recur, though: the kit semi_truck hero (a van and truck deck sits in the window, and no. 41 shot the same kit truck), lengths at one scale as a bar (no. 42's measured columns) and a Blackland clay Texas relief (no. 44's clay register). Fresh concept, more than one familiar move.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Twenty front-on bobtails in a thin band read as icons. The lower quarter is a dark dead zone, and the horizon tonal step sits behind dek lines 2 and 3.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Keep the frontal azimuth that shows all 20, but dolly the camera in about 35 percent and tilt down so the near rank's bumpers land at design y about 1150 and fill the lower half. Lower the far ground's fog so the horizon step falls below the dek's last line.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The loss bar is a flat pebbled navy rectangle with a stray mid-height hairline. The billet is a 14 px sliver, an empty band runs from y 700 to 1000, and the $9M tick's zero is off frame because the datum bleeds left.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Shorten the datum so its left end and the billet sit in frame at design x about 80, with the $9M tick scribed from that visible end, delete the leftover hairline, and show the bar's lit top face and long cast.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The rule reads as six flat mid-grey tiles under a bracket. The grooves have no visible depth and the face sits in the grey middle.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Cut the week grooves three times deeper and half as wide, and drop the key elevation so each groove's left wall goes black and its right lip takes a specular line while the face itself falls dark.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A lavender-blue key on the cab and trailer lights the camera-left flank. The trailer front is a flat primitive slab across the left third, and the beacon dome is dimmer than the headlamp.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Neutralise the sky IBL tint and swing the camera to the cab's right front quarter so the declared key rakes the hood and right flank, and raise the beacon's emissive until the dome is the brightest form in the frame.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The right half is dark asphalt with a lone yellow bollard, and the boom shows no pivot or cabinet.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Stand the guard_gate's pivot cabinet on the lit concrete pad at the right edge, with the boom springing from it.
